title: feat(client): coalesce adjacent ranges in GcsBidiReadChannel.readVectored()
hypothesis: GcsBidiReadChannel.readVectored() issues one BlobReadSession.readAs() per range while GcsReadChannel (HTTP) coalesces adjacent ranges with VectoredIoUtil.mergeGcsObjectRanges() per GcsVectoredReadOptions. title: feat(core): serve vectored tail ranges from the cached footer in GcsFooterOptimizer

title: fix(client): short-circuit zero-length vectored ranges and validate offsets up front
hypothesis: A zero-length GcsObjectRange passed to GcsBidiReadChannel.readVectored() becomes RangeSpec.of(offset, 0), which java-storage interprets as 'read to EOF', so the caller receives the whole object tail instead of an empty buffer; GcsReadChannel opens an unnecessary ranged RPC for the same input, and a negative offset/length in the bidi path throws mid-loop leaving sibling futures hanging. Validating ranges up front and short-circuiting zero-length ranges with an empty buffer aligns both transports with the Hadoop/Iceberg tail-range edge cases.
learning: java-storage RangeSpec.of(offset, 0) means read-to-EOF: zero-length vectored ranges on the bidi path returned the whole object tail. Fixed with a shared VectoredIoUtil pre-validation helper (6 files/271 lines). Draft PR #406.

title: perf(client): avoid O(N^2) copying in VectoredIoUtil.mergeGcsObjectRanges
hypothesis: Accumulating merged underlying ranges lazily in a single ImmutableList.Builder per combined group inside VectoredIoUtil.mergeGcsObjectRanges (instead of calling GcsObjectCombinedRange.union on every step, which copies all prior ranges into a new ImmutableList and AutoValue instance each iteration) and using a static Comparator with ImmutableList.sortedCopyOf reduces range coalescing from O(N^2) time and allocation to O(N), proven by VectoredRangeCoalescingBenchmark.

Improved all 9 VectoredRangeCoalescingBenchmark cases: up to -99.0% latency (2.71ms -> 27.2us, 100x faster) and -99.8% allocation (39.7MB -> 92.2KiB, 430x less memory) at ranges=4096, plus -21% to -44% on unmerged gapBytes=1048576 cases.

learning: PR #441 review feedback [@gemini-code-assist[bot] (common/src/test/java/com/google/cloud/gcs/analyticscore/common/cache/AnalyticsCacheCaffeineImplTest.java:108): ![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)  Busy-waiting using a spin loop (`Thread.onSpinWait()`) with a very short duration (1,000 nanoseconds) is highly prone to flakiness in virtualized CI/CD environments due to CPU scheduling, GC pauses, and coarse system timer resolutions.  Using `TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS` with a short `Thread.sleep(10)` is much more robust, consumes no CPU while waiting, and ensures the entry has expired across all platforms.  ```java   void createWithTtlOnly_expiredEntry_evictsOnCleanUp() throws InterruptedException {     AnalyticsCacheCaffeineImpl<String, String> ttlCache =         AnalyticsCacheCaffeineImpl.createWithTtlOnly(1, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);      ttlCache.put("key1", "value1");     Thread.sleep(10);     ttlCache.cleanUp();      assertThat(ttlCache.get("key1")).isEmpty();     assertThat(ttlCache.size()).isEqualTo(0);   } ```] -> Resolution: #4411085673: Declined based on monotonic clock determinism and repo hygiene constraints:  1. **Clock-Source Identity**: `AnalyticsCacheCaffeineImpl.createWithTtlOnly` configures Caffeine with its default `Ticker.systemTicker()`, which reads `System.nanoTime()`—the exact same monotonic clock polled by the `while (System.nanoTime() - start < 1_000L)` spin loop on the same thread. Because the TTL is 1 ns and the loop only exits when `System.nanoTime() - start >= 1_000 ns`, followed by synchronous `cleanUp()` acquiring `evictionLock.lock()`, eviction is mathematically guaranteed. CPU preemption, hypervisor scheduling delays, and GC pauses only increase elapsed monotonic time, pushing the entry further past its 1 ns TTL (non-expiry is tested separately with a 1-hour TTL). 2. **Hygiene Gate Compliance**: Repository guardrails in `.sil/loop.yaml` explicitly forbid `Thread.sleep(` under `hygiene.forbid_added_patterns` to prevent sleep-induced latency in the test suite. In contrast, the 1 µs `Thread.onSpinWait()` loop executes in ~0.001 ms without kernel context switching.
